cli.stdio: The child inherits stdin, stdout and stderr as byte streams; the runner does not decode or buffer them.
cli.stdout: Reserved for child output, including when config or spawn fails.
cli.diagnostics: Runner diagnostics, including --json run errors, go to stderr. --quiet suppresses the run summary.
cli.normalExit: Return the child's numeric exit status unchanged.
cli.posixChildSignal: Terminate the runner with the same signal, preserving signal identity for its parent.
cli.posixParentSignal: Forward SIGINT or SIGTERM, allow up to five seconds for shutdown, then terminate the runner with the first requested signal. Further requests do not extend grace. With all three streams non-TTY, signal and clean up the entire owned child process group, even after its leader exits; SIGKILL remaining members at the deadline. Ordinary child completion does not trigger group cleanup and descendants that leave the group are excluded.
cli.posixTerminalSignal: Interactive children retain the inherited group and terminal stdin access. When the group owns the foreground terminal, do not relay SIGINT already delivered by Ctrl+C; SIGINT sent only to the runner PID is likewise not relayed because its source cannot be distinguished portably. SIGTERM is forwarded to the direct child. Timeout SIGKILL targets only the child, never the shared terminal group.
cli.windows: Return the available numeric child status; POSIX signal identity and process groups do not apply. Batch files use the Windows command processor.

nodeApi.runWithInjectedEnv: Promise<number>: normal status unchanged, spawn failure 126/127, signal termination 128 plus the platform signal number.
nodeApi.runWithInjectedEnvDetailed: Promise<{ exitCode: number | null, signal: NodeJS.Signals | null, spawnError?: { code: string, message: string, exitStatus: 126 | 127 } }>.
nodeApi.spawnWithInjectedEnv: Returns the child process and its completion promise. stdio defaults to inherit; pipe makes stdin, stdout and stderr available to the caller.
